title: Audit existing code: a review standard an agent can apply line by line
summary: An agent reviews source code that already exists, such as a pull request or an inherited chat UI, against the contracts for the patterns it contains, and returns a verdict per rule with the line that proves or breaks it.

persona.role: Engineer reviewing AI interface code written by someone else, or by an agent
persona.context: A streaming chat view shipped before any of this existed. An accessibility complaint has arrived and nobody knows what the component was supposed to guarantee.
persona.goal: A short list of the rules the code breaks, each with a line number, a reason, and a test that would have caught it.

trigger: They tell the agent: "Review this streaming response component. What does it get wrong?"

advantage.claim: Review comments that cite a rule, a reason, and a test, not a reviewer's taste.
advantage.why_it_holds: Every constraint has a stable id, a level, a rationale, and a verification note, so a finding can be stated as a violated rule. Storybook and Figma servers describe what exists; the HAX workbook is an exercise for a human team. None hands an agent a standard to judge code against.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).
A scratch project to hold the code under review.

steps.action: Set up the code under review. For an unattended run, take the reference streaming component as the inherited code.
steps.expect: The component source, to be copied into the workspace as inherited/ChatStream.tsx.

steps.action: Seed one known defect so the audit has something it must find.

uses.change: Write the copy from s1, then remove the attributes role="status", aria-live="polite", and aria-atomic="true" from the visually hidden announcement element. Change nothing else.

steps.expect: A component that no longer announces completion to assistive technology and otherwise behaves as before.

steps.action: From here on, act as a reviewer who has not seen s1 or s2. Identify which pattern the code implements by describing what it does.

input.query: render model output progressively as tokens arrive with a stop control

steps.action: Fetch the full rules, with the verification note for each.
steps.expect: A constraints array. The returned files are not used and must not be compared with the code under review.

steps.action: Judge the code against each MUST and MUST_NOT.
steps.expect: For every rule: pass, fail, or unknown, with the file and line that supports it. Unknown is allowed; a pass without a cited line is not.

uses.change: Findings ordered MUST_NOT and MUST first. Each finding: constraint id, level, the line, the contract's rationale in one sentence, the smallest fix, and the name of the test that should be added, in the form "<constraint-id>: <behavior>".

steps.expect: A review the author of the code could act on without asking a question.

success.criterion: The seeded defect is found and attributed to the right rule.
success.check: AUDIT.md reports a failure under completion-announced that points at the announcement element in inherited/ChatStream.tsx.

success.criterion: No rule is passed on faith.
success.check: Every pass in AUDIT.md cites a file and line. Rules the reviewer could not settle from the source are marked unknown.
No MUST-level rule other than completion-announced is reported as a failure.

success.criterion: Every finding names the test that would have caught it.
success.check: Each failure in AUDIT.md includes a proposed test name starting with the constraint id.

gaps.summary: The catalog has no way to say "check this code". An agent must discover that scaffold_pattern is how to read a contract, then ignore the files it generates.
gaps.evidence: The server exposes exactly two tools, search_patterns and scaffold_pattern. A check_consistency tool is listed as deferred in PROGRESS.md to hold the two-tool cap.
gaps.fix: Either lift the cap for a third tool, or deliver the audit as a published skill that carries this procedure and uses the two existing tools. The contract-auditor subagent in .claude/agents/ is the internal version of that skill.

automation.schedule: On demand, and as the prompt behind a pull-request review for repositories that adopted a pattern.
automation.notes: The seeded defect makes the run self-checking. For real use, skip s1 and s2 and point the agent at the code to review. For a running UI with no source access, use probe-a-running-ui instead.
